correctness.rationale: An explicit bitmask algorithm exhausts all 252 possible five-cuts of KG(5,2), yielding 120 facets and 495 faces. All 237 discrete-Morse pairs are validated as acyclic by topological sorting all 495 nodes and 1850 Hasse edges. Complete signed integral chain cancellation uses 237 unit pivots, leaving a CW complex with one 0-cell, eight 3-cells and twelve 4-cells. The exact 8x12 attaching matrix has rank 7 and an integer 7x7 minor equal to 1, hence seven Smith units and no torsion. Since pi_3 of a wedge of eight 3-spheres is Z^8, the attaching maps are classified by this integral matrix; unimodular changes yield S^3 wedge five S^4. Independent unreduced chain-rank calculations over five finite fields reproduce Betti ranks; mod-p agreement is not substituted for the integral proof.

originality.rationale: The arXiv primary texts and indexed related claims do not imply the five-cut Petersen homotopy type: Bayer et al. explicitly treat Petersen at cut size two; their complete-skeleton theorem is inapplicable at size five since only 200 of 210 tetrahedra occur. The sequel studies disjoint unions, squared paths and grids; a known indexed five-cut result concerns a 3-by-3 grid rather than Petersen, and an indexed high-girth result requires girth at least seven for five-cuts. Distinct four-cut, three-cut, total-cut and matching-complex results cannot determine this complex from wording or inclusion alone. An unindexed equivalent calculation remains a risk.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical symmetric graph of girth five, and the cut threshold five is intrinsic rather than an arbitrary slice: it meets its girth and is half its vertex count. The exact mixed-dimensional integral homotopy type distinguishes two nontrivial homological degrees, determines all torsion and attaching maps, and proves nonshellability of the pure 4-complex. This fills a concrete boundary case not subsumed by published cut-complex classifications, potentially informing further threshold studies; no unsupported general theorem is claimed.
